bc_grad_wall.blurb: A bolted wall of about 50 m on the lower southwest slopes of Mount Sentinel, above Castlegar in the West Kootenays. Most of the twelve climbs are one or two pitches of sport, with a couple of trad lines, and the grades sit mainly around 5.10 with a handful of easier lines starting near 5.7 and a single 5.11. The stone is compact and nicely featured. Because it looks southwest it picks up the sun in the afternoon and shrugs off rain quickly, which makes it a decent shoulder-season choice. Open grassy benches sit at the base and the descent is a simple walk. Expect bears, ticks and poison ivy in the warm months. A 70 m rope is handy.
bc_grad_wall.parking_note: Drive north from Castlegar on Highway 3A, cross the Brilliant Bridge, and turn onto Robson Access Road. After roughly 1.2 km take Terrace Road and pull onto the wide gravel shoulder about 300 m up, which fits a few vehicles.
bc_grad_wall.approach: A steep, faint climber's trail of roughly 15 to 20 minutes climbs a grassy bowl. Cross a deep ditch, follow the gas line west for about 50 m, then turn uphill and keep left at the trail split to reach the open bench under the wall.

bc_psyche_slab.blurb: A big, low-angle face in the Eldred Valley near Powell River, and the busiest wall in a remote valley. The climbing is long slab routes, mostly traditional with a little bolted protection, running from about 5.6 up to 5.11, with most lines clustered around 5.10 and a few moderate options. Many routes go for four to twelve pitches, so this is a place for full days rather than quick laps. Lower pitches can be mossy or dirty, so a brush and sticky smearing shoes help. Plan carefully, since the valley is far from town.
